answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes. Consider a juniper at the center, a forge resting nearby, and a sable beyond the hills: three anchors, none forged, all earned over time.
